description.sr_latin: Kratke, ponovljive rečenice koje pokazuju kako se sklapaju misli — hoću, mogu, moram, idem, daj mi.
description.en: Short, reusable sentence frames that show how thoughts get assembled — want, can, must, go, give me. Swap the fillers and say almost anything.

phrases.context: Tell your girlfriend you're ready to crash for the night.
phrases.notes: The core frame: 'Hoću da' + verb in the present = 'I want to ___'. Serbian has no infinitive here — you literally say 'I want that I sleep'.

phrases.en: I don't want to get up.
phrases.context: Groan this to your girlfriend on a lazy weekend morning.
phrases.notes: 'Neću' is the negated 'hoću' — one word, not 'ne hoću'. Same 'da' + verb frame.

phrases.context: Ask your girlfriend if she's hungry too.
phrases.notes: 'Hoćeš da ...?' is the everyday way to suggest doing something together — softer than a command.

phrases.context: Offer a hand to your friend who's stuck with something.
phrases.notes: 'Pomoći' takes the dative, so 'ti' (to you). Clitic order: 'da ti pomognem'.

phrases.context: Ask your friend for a hand carrying something.
phrases.notes: 'Možeš li ...?' = 'can you ...?'. The little 'li' makes it a question. 'Mi' (to me) is dative because 'pomoći' needs it.

phrases.context: Explain to your girlfriend why you can't hang out right now.
phrases.notes: 'Moram da' + verb = 'I have to ___'. Strong obligation.

phrases.context: Nag your friend who skipped lunch again.
Tell your friend it's time for you to head off.
phrases.notes: 'Treba da' + verb = 'I should / ought to ___'. 'Treba' stays in the 3rd person — it doesn't change for the subject.

phrases.context: Admit to your friend that you're stuck.
phrases.notes: Different frame: 'treba mi X' = 'I need X' (literally 'X is needed to me'). The thing you need is the subject; you are the dative 'mi'.

phrases.context: Tell your girlfriend you're parched.
Wave off your girlfriend offering you food or drink.
phrases.notes: Here 'hteti' takes a direct object instead of 'da'. Double negative is normal: 'neću ništa' (lit. 'I-won't nothing').

phrases.context: Ask your girlfriend to pass the water at dinner.
phrases.notes: 'Daj mi' + thing = 'give me ___'. 'Vode' is genitive ('some water', a partial amount) — very natural for food and drink.

phrases.context: Point at something and ask your friend to hand it over.
Ask your girlfriend to pass the bread across the table.
phrases.notes: 'Dodaj' (from 'dodati') is specifically 'pass / hand over', perfect at the table.

phrases.context: Ask your girlfriend to bring you a glass from the kitchen.
phrases.notes: 'Donesi' = bring (it here). Genitive 'vode' again signals 'some water'.

phrases.context: Ask your friend to grab the coffees from the counter.
Check if your friend is free for a coffee.
phrases.notes: 'Imaš li ...?' = 'do you have ...?'. After this kind of question the noun often goes genitive: 'vremena'.

phrases.context: Ask your friend if there's coffee at his place.
Ask your girlfriend where she put the bottle.
phrases.notes: 'Gde je ___?' = 'where is ___?'. Swap in any noun.

phrases.en: Shall we go for a beer?
phrases.context: Suggest grabbing a drink with your friend after work.
phrases.notes: 'Idemo na ___?' = 'shall we go for ___?'. Use 'na' + accusative for activities: 'na pivo', 'na kafu', 'na ručak'.

phrases.context: Ask your girlfriend nicely from the couch.
phrases.notes: Politer than the bare imperative 'donesi'. Combines 'možeš li da' with the bring-frame.

phrases.context: Tell your girlfriend you're heading out for a bit.
phrases.notes: 'Idem u' + place (accusative) = 'I'm going to ___'. Motion toward a place uses 'u' + accusative.

phrases.context: Tell your friend you're heading home for the night.
phrases.notes: 'Kući' is a fixed form meaning 'home(ward)' — no preposition needed.

phrases.context: Tell your girlfriend you're off to grab some food.
phrases.notes: 'Idem da' + verb = 'I'm going (in order) to ___'. Expresses purpose.

phrases.context: Tell your friend you're heading to the café.
phrases.notes: For activities and events Serbian uses 'na' + accusative: 'na kafu', 'na pivo', 'na ručak'.

phrases.context: Call your girlfriend to the table.
phrases.notes: 'Hajde da' + we-form = 'let's ___'. The verb takes the 'we' ending ('jedemo').

phrases.context: Nudge your friend that it's time to leave.
Text your girlfriend to ask when she'll be back.
phrases.notes: Imperfective 'dolaziš' fits a general 'are you coming (tonight)?' question.

phrases.en: I'll be there in five minutes.
phrases.context: Text your friend that you're almost at the meeting spot.
phrases.notes: 'Za' + time = 'in / within (that much time)'. After 'pet' (5+) the noun goes genitive plural: 'minuta'.

phrases.context: Tell your girlfriend you're just stepping out for a second.
phrases.notes: Reflexive 'se' stays attached. 'Odmah' = right away / immediately.

phrases.context: Sign off with your friend after a chat.
phrases.notes: 'Vidimo se' = 'we'll see each other' (reflexive). Add 'kasnije' (later), 'sutra' (tomorrow), 'veceras' (tonight).

phrases.context: Text your girlfriend that you're already at the restaurant.
phrases.notes: 'Čekati' takes a direct object (accusative), so 'te' (you) — no preposition, unlike English 'wait FOR'.

phrases.en: What do you want to do?
phrases.context: Ask your girlfriend how she wants to spend the evening.
phrases.notes: 'Šta hoćeš da ...?' = 'what do you want (us/me) to ...?'. The verb after 'da' takes a personal ending — here 'radimo' (we).

phrases.context: Check in on your girlfriend who seems off.
phrases.notes: 'Jesi li ...?' is the full-verb question form of 'si'. 'Jesi li dobro?' = 'are you okay/well?'.

phrases.en: Do you want to come with me?
phrases.context: Invite your girlfriend along when you're heading out.
phrases.notes: 'Hoćeš li ...?' = 'do you want ...?'. 'Sa mnom' = 'with me' (instrumental of 'ja'). 'Sa' takes the instrumental case.

phrases.context: Wish your girlfriend goodnight.
phrases.notes: 'Lepo' here is the adverb 'nicely / well'. A warm bedtime line.

phrases.context: Joke with your friend about being a heavy sleeper.
phrases.notes: 'Volim da' + verb = 'I love (doing) ___'. A habit or general liking.

phrases.en: I love it when you're here.
phrases.context: Tell your girlfriend something sweet at home.
phrases.notes: 'Volim kad ...' = 'I love it when ...'. 'Kad' (when) introduces the situation; 'tu' = here/around.

phrases.en: I hate it when you're late.
phrases.context: Tease your friend who always shows up late.
phrases.notes: Mirror of 'volim kad'. 'Kasniš' = 'you're (running) late' (from 'kasniti').

phrases.context: Ask your friend if he wants to grab food.
phrases.notes: Say 'gladna' to a woman: 'Jesi li gladna?'. Adjective agrees with the listener's gender.

phrases.context: Confirm evening plans with your girlfriend.
Agree to your friend's suggestion.
phrases.notes: Literally 'it's possible', but used constantly as 'okay / works for me / sure'.

phrases.context: Ask your girlfriend to wait a second while you finish something.
phrases.notes: 'Samo malo' literally 'only a little' — the everyday 'hang on a sec / one moment'.

phrases.context: Reassure your girlfriend after a tiny mix-up.
phrases.notes: Lit. 'it's not terrible'. A warm 'no big deal / don't worry about it'. 'Nije' is the negative of 'je' (is).

phrases.en: Get in touch. / Let me know.
phrases.context: Tell your friend to message you when he's free.
phrases.notes: 'Javiti se' = to get in touch / drop a line. 'Javi mi se' = 'let me know / hit me up'. The 'se' belongs to the verb; 'mi' = to me.

phrases.context: React warmly to good news from your girlfriend.
phrases.notes: 'Baš' intensifies — 'really / so'. 'Baš lepo' = 'that's really nice'.

phrases.context: Tell your friend to slow down and relax.
phrases.notes: Quintessentially Serbian — 'polako' means 'slowly / easy / no rush'. Both a reply and a whole philosophy.

phrases.context: Answer your girlfriend's 'will you?' with an easy yes.
Brush off your friend's apology for being late.
phrases.notes: 'Nema' = 'there isn't'. The thing that isn't there goes genitive: 'problema'.

phrases.context: Shrug at your friend's question.
phrases.notes: Very common shrug. 'Pojma' (of a clue/idea) is genitive after the negative 'nemam'.
